substantiveness.reason: The target is a real conditional bound. Its conclusion (formal/nightstream-fprime/tests/EvidenceTargets.lean:290-304) bounds the actual accepted-terminal mass by returned-advice mass plus, per visit, marked-collision mass + goodActive - g(Q_j, goodActive) + deltaFS(Q_j) + weakLoss + testError + 17 * actual adaptive MSIS success. With g(Q,p)=p the conclusion is a knowledge-soundness bound that is not provable without the FS premise. The premise is satisfiable and not vacuous: WideFiatShamir.FiatShamirModel (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Lifecycle/Nifs/WideFiatShamir.lean:108-112) is one inequality on real numbers; the other premises (depth bound, storage bound, summability, LowNormInvertibility, Bounded, instances) are the same satisfiable premises as the old target. The accepted event target.Holds (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Export/Stage1/Wide/TerminalSecurity.lean:73-75) is not empty (the bottom envelope at iteration 0 is accepted, formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Lifecycle/Stage1/Terminal.lean:84-92). The real-success event is not empty or free: it is proved equal to the goodActive mass (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Export/Stage1/HyperNovaVisitedAcceptance.lean:206-222). The MSIS term is the computed reduction's success, not a free parameter (EvidenceTargets.lean:301-304).

findings.text: The instance binders and the interactive terms name ProductionKey.key, not the wide key. This is sound because the wide key overrides only piRlcResponse and piRlcResponseValid and the interactive chain reads neither. A reader can mistake this for use of the retired narrow sampler. FIAT_SHAMIR_MODEL.md:108-111 explains it.

The bound is parametric in g and deltaFS. With g = 0 and deltaFS = 0 the premise can hold and the conclusion is weak. This is inherent to the approved parametric FS boundary (FIAT_SHAMIR_MODEL.md:60-65), not a defect of the target.
